To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

barriers to early diagnosis and treatment include: (1) a lack of knowledge about breast cancer, its risk factors and early detection, (2) a lack of access to screening, (3) a lack of trust in the healthcare system, and (4) a lack of social and economic support.

barriers to early detection of breast cancer in Kenya include: 1. The stigma associated with breast cancer, 2. Lack of access to health care services, 3. Lack of awareness about early detection, and 4. Lack of knowledge of breast cancer risk factors and symptoms.
barriers to breast cancer screening in Kenya include lack of awareness, fear, and stigma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the barriers and facilitators of breast cancer early detection and treatment in Kenya, and the role of community health workers in addressing them.
understanding how women with breast cancer in the Kenyan context make sense of their diagnosis and treatment and the barriers and facilitators to early detection and engagement in treatment.
the identification of barriers and facilitators of breast cancer screening and subsequent treatment engagement in Kenya.

the study has been successful in its attempt at providing an in depth analysis of the factors influencing the uptake of breast cancer screening in Kenya.
there is no evidence that the use of breast self-examination (BSE) increases the likelihood of early diagnosis of breast cancer.

the study has shown that the barriers to early breast cancer detection and treatment engagement are lack of awareness and knowledge, fear and anxiety, lack of screening facilities and lack of screening facilities in rural areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a number of barriers and facilitators that are unique to breast cancer in Kenya and that may also be relevant to breast cancer in other LMIC.
we have developed an innovative approach for identifying the barriers and facilitators to breast cancer early detection and subsequent treatment in Kenya.

there is a need for a more comprehensive approach to addressing breast cancer early detection and subsequent treatment in Kenya, and this should include the following: 1) a more robust and sustainable screening infrastructure, 2) a more robust health care infrastructure, 3) more comprehensive health education, 4) more comprehensive health policy, 5) more comprehensive community engagement, and 6) more comprehensive health research.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are many barriers to early diagnosis and treatment of breast cancer in Kenya, including lack of knowledge about early diagnosis and treatment, lack of access to health care, lack of access and availability of health care, lack and availability of health services, and lack and availability of treatment.
there is a need to improve the quality of breast health services in Kenya, and that the quality of services provided is a key determinant in whether a woman seeks breast health services.

the Kenyan government and other stakeholders should consider implementing a national screening program to improve early detection of breast cancer and increase the number of women who are treated for breast cancer in Kenya.
